statement: The maximum number of real projective lines on a nonsingular real cubic surface is 27, attained by species I.1.

source.location: Art 5, first case A, printed p.197
source.version: Original Philosophical Transactions 153(1863),193–241; JSTOR original-journal scan

scope: Nonsingular real cubic surfaces in real projective three-space; count real projective lines, not only lines with a specified affine incidence.
notes:
The five-species source analysis includes generic canonical forms; modern all-smooth formulations are separate literature.

The 1863 paper explicitly states that its nonsingular-cubic theory reproduces and develops Schläfli’s 1858 article. The earlier attribution is included; the 1863 text remains the inspected classification source.

Related literature. An attempt to determine the twenty-seven lines upon a surface of the third order, and to divide such surfaces into species in reference to the reality of the lines upon the surface (Ludwig Schläfli, 1858). Historical or related contributions are retained here. Their own precise statements have not been independently verified for a separate result in this migration.

Source discussion. Species I.1 has all 27 lines real; the complex count gives the matching upper bound.
